# Frozen seasonal observer references â€” 2026-11-04

Thirty-six original NASA/JPL Horizons text responses contain 432 observations:
four existing sites, nine bodies and 12 monthly 2026 epochs. The exact input plan,
quantities, calendar/time interpretation, fixed acceptance controls and actual
requests were frozen before capture. No model values are stored as references.

The first research capture stopped after six responses on an incorrect assumption
that every Earth-center header used DE441. The original independent baseline
already retained Jupiter/Neptune kernel-specific Earth centers. The explicit
admission amendment binds those per-body identities, preserves the original
failure/six responses and fetches only the remaining 30 queries. No query/date,
site, quantity, model or numerical budget changed. The sixth capture's time is
bounded by the original interval rather than an invented exact instant.

The original and amended helpers are preserved as text only. Admission must never
execute them. Both acquisition states remain original; captured_not_qualified
describes capture rather than a scientific accuracy certification.

The CSV is derived from raw Q2/Q4/Q20/Q49 rows, with both requested and returned
JD/UT values and exact raw-response hashes. Distances use 149597870.7 km per au.
The crate copy must match exactly. Source kernels, observer, airless convention,
API version, unit header, epoch order and finite quantity domains remain explicit.

These are sampled seasonal references, not continuous/full-span qualification,
event timing, physical visibility or navigation evidence. Future EOP samples are
predictions. Planetary and catalogue-moon validity claims remain separate.

Public US government source data are attributed to NASA/JPL Horizons. No project
licensing declaration is changed. Original source documentation:
https://ssd-api.jpl.nasa.gov/doc/horizons.html#tlist-parameter
https://ssd.jpl.nasa.gov/horizons/manual.html
